sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.license_note: United States government publication; verify notices in the source before redistribution.
sources.summary: Voluntary guidance for managing risks to individuals, organisations and society across AI system design, development, deployment and use. Organised around Govern, Map, Measure and Manage.
not_for: treating every data product as an AI system
making AI mandatory in the Core

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.license_note: United States government publication; verify notices in the source before redistribution.
sources.summary: A companion resource to the AI RMF that identifies risks particular to generative AI and actions organisations can take to manage them.
not_for: assuming generative AI and autonomous agents are equivalent

sources.title: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.license_note: United States government publication; verify notices in the source before redistribution.
sources.summary: Outcome-oriented cybersecurity risk guidance structured around Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover.

sources.title: NIST Privacy Framework: A Tool for Improving Privacy through Enterprise Risk Management
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.license_note: United States government publication; verify notices in the source before redistribution.
sources.summary: A voluntary enterprise risk framework for identifying and managing privacy risk through the data processing lifecycle.
not_for: claiming compliance with a privacy law
assuming version 1.0 is the latest draft activity

sources.title: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.license_note: United States government publication; verify incorporated material and notices before redistribution.
sources.summary: A catalog of security and privacy controls for information systems and organisations, including control assessment and system lifecycle concerns.
not_for: requiring the full catalog in every organisation

sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) - Version 3
sources.license_note: Subject to the W3C document license and notices in the specification.
sources.summary: An RDF vocabulary for interoperability between data catalogs, covering datasets, data services, distributions, catalog records and related resources.
not_for: equating a dataset record with a complete data product contract

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.license_note: Subject to the W3C document license and notices in the specification.
sources.summary: An OWL2 ontology for representing provenance information using entities, activities, agents and their relationships.
not_for: proving truth merely because provenance metadata exists

sources.title: Data on the Web Best Practices: Data Quality Vocabulary
sources.license_note: Subject to the W3C document license and notices in the note.
sources.summary: A vocabulary for expressing data quality metadata, measurements, metrics, policies and quality annotations.
not_for: asserting that a quality target proves measured quality

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.license_note: Subject to the W3C document license and notices in the specification.
sources.summary: An information model and vocabulary for expressing permissions, prohibitions, duties and constraints in policies.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.license_note: Subject to the W3C document license and notices in the specification.
sources.summary: A common RDF data model for representing and linking thesauri, taxonomies, classification schemes and other knowledge organisation systems.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.license_note: Subject to the W3C document license and notices in the specification.
sources.summary: A language for describing and validating constraints over RDF graphs through reusable shapes.
not_for: requiring RDF validation in all implementations
treating successful validation as proof of business value

sources.title: OECD AI Principles
sources.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
sources.license_note: OECD terms apply; do not redistribute full text without permission.
sources.summary: Intergovernmental principles for trustworthy AI and policy recommendations, updated in 2024 to address technical and policy developments.
not_for: making all AI-specific practices Core requirements

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
sources.license_note: EU reuse rules and source notices apply; retain official-source attribution.
sources.summary: European Union regulation establishing harmonised rules for AI systems using a risk-based legal framework and phased application.
use_for: risk-management, documentation, oversight and monitoring concepts
not_for: assuming every agent use is a high-risk AI system

sources.title: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship
sources.license_note: Article published under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; preserve attribution and indicate changes.
sources.summary: Original peer-reviewed statement of principles intended to make digital research objects findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable, with emphasis on machine actionability.
not_for: equating FAIR objects with governed data products

sources.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Management system
sources.license_note: Copyright ISO; catalog metadata and official landing-page reference only unless separately licensed.
sources.summary: An AI management system standard for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving organisational governance of AI systems.
not_for: quoting or reproducing paid standard text

sources.title: Data Management Capability Assessment Model (DCAM)
sources.license_note: EDM Council intellectual property; official overview metadata only unless separately licensed.
sources.summary: A professional capability assessment model for data management, used here only as a potential comparison point for operating practices and assessment coverage.
